nodes.summary: Backward equations for the mean hitting time (compare Norris 1997, §3.3): if `m : ι → ℝ` is nonnegative and `(Q m) i = -1` for `i ∉ A`, then `E_i H_A ≤ m i` (so it is finite), `E_i H_A = 0` on `A`, and the real vector `E_i H_A` solves the same backward equations. With uniqueness of the solution, this identifies `E_i H_A`.
nodes.title: Backward equations for the mean hitting time

nodes.summary: From a state `i ∉ A`, the hitting time of `A` is the first holding time plus the hitting time of the chain restarted after the first jump.
nodes.title: First-jump decomposition of a hitting time

nodes.summary: From a state `i ∈ A`, the hitting time of `A` is `0` as soon as the first holding time is positive (which fails only on a null event, see `ctmcHoldingTime`).
nodes.title: Hitting time from inside the target set is zero

nodes.summary: Let `mA`, `mB`, `f` be nonnegative with `(Q mA) i = -1` off `A`, `(Q mB) i = -1` off `B` and `(Q f) i = -(mA i + mB i)` off `A ∪ B`. Then `E_i (H_A H_B) ≤ f i` (so it is finite), it is `0` on `A ∪ B`, and its real part `p` solves `(Q p) i = -(E_i H_A + E_i H_B)` off `A ∪ B`.
nodes.title: Backward equations for the product moment of two hitting times

nodes.summary: The hitting time `inf {t ≥ 0 | X t ∈ A}` of a set of states `A` by the chain `X = ctmcPath Q i ω` started at `i`, valued in `ℝ≥0∞` (it is `∞` if `A` is never visited).
nodes.title: Hitting time of a continuous-time Markov chain

nodes.summary: Minimality of the mean hitting time (compare Norris 1997, §3.3): if every state off `A` has a positive exit rate, every `m : ι → ℝ≥0∞` with `1 / q i + ∑ⱼ Π i j m j ≤ m i` off `A` dominates `E_i H_A`.
nodes.title: Minimality of the mean hitting time

nodes.summary: If `mA`, `mB` are supersolutions of the mean equations of `A` and `B` (as in `lintegral_ctmcHittingTime_le`) and `F` satisfies `(mA i + mB i) / q i + ∑ⱼ Π i j F j ≤ F i` off `A ∪ B`, then `F` dominates `E_i (H_A H_B)`.
nodes.title: Minimality of the product moment

nodes.summary: From a state of `A ∪ B`, the product moment of the hitting times of `A` and `B` is `0`.
nodes.title: Product moment of hitting times from inside their union is zero

nodes.summary: From `i ∉ A ∪ B` with `q i ≠ 0`, `E_i (H_A H_B) = (E_i H_A + E_i H_B) / q i + ∑ⱼ Π i j E_j (H_A H_B)` in `ℝ≥0∞`.
nodes.title: Product moment of two hitting times, first-step equation

nodes.summary: From a state of `A`, the mean hitting time of `A` is `0`.
nodes.title: Mean hitting time from inside the target set is zero

nodes.summary: Mean hitting time, first-step equation (compare Norris 1997, §3.3): from `i ∉ A` with `q i = -Q i i ≠ 0`, `E_i H_A = 1 / q i + ∑ⱼ Π i j E_j H_A` in `ℝ≥0∞`.
nodes.title: Mean hitting time, first-step equation
